<!-- Generated by docs/scripts/generate_reference.py from the code. Do not edit by hand. -->

The target is the model or agent under test. It is described the same way every model in a campaign is: a name, how to reach it, and how to sample from it.

The same shape describes attack roles, judges, guardrails and the goal classifier, so once you can write a target you can write all of them.

## `target` {#modelconfig}

A model HackAgent talks to: its name, how to reach it, and how to sample from
it.

The same shape describes the target, every attack helper (role), every judge,
every guardrail and the goal classifier.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string (at least 1) | **required** | The model to use, as the provider names it, e.g. `gpt-4o-mini` or `llama3`. Also used to label the model in results. |
| `connection` | [ConnectionSpec](#connectionspec) | **required** | How to reach the model. |
| `generation` | [GenerationSpec](#generationspec) | see [GenerationSpec](#generationspec) | Sampling settings for every request. |
| `options` | map of string to any | empty | Settings specific to one kind of agent that are neither connection nor sampling, e.g. the `binary` path of a CLI agent, ADK's `user_id`, or a web target's CSS selectors. |

## `target.connection` {#connectionspec}

How to reach a model: which client to use, where it lives, and how to
authenticate.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `provider` | string (at least 1) | **required** | A label for who serves the model (`openai`, `ollama`, `vllm`, `local`…). Informational only: launch tooling reads it, but the request path uses `type`. |
| `type` | [agent type](#agent-types) | **required** | Which client talks to the model. This is the field that matters: it decides whether HackAgent calls a chat API (`OPENAI_SDK`, `OLLAMA`, `LITELLM`…) or drives an agent directly (`CLAUDE_CODE`, `GOOGLE_ADK`, `WEB`…). |
| `endpoint` | string | unset | Base URL of the model's API, e.g. `http://localhost:11434` for Ollama. Leave unset for local agents such as `CLAUDE_CODE`, which run on this machine. |
| `api_key_env` | string | unset | Name of the environment variable that holds the API key, e.g. `OPENAI_API_KEY`. The key itself never goes in the campaign file. |
| `headers` | map of string to string | empty | Extra HTTP headers sent with every request. |
| `timeout` | number (> 0) | `120.0` | Seconds to wait for one reply before giving up. |

## `target.generation` {#generationspec}

Sampling settings applied to every request the model receives. All optional:
anything left unset uses the provider's own default.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_tokens` | integer (>= 1) | unset | Longest reply, in tokens. |
| `temperature` | number (>= 0.0) | unset | Randomness of the reply. `0` is the most deterministic. |
| `top_p` | number (>= 0.0, <= 1.0) | unset | Nucleus sampling: only consider the most likely tokens whose probabilities add up to this value. |
| `frequency_penalty` | number | unset | Discourage repeating the same tokens. |
| `presence_penalty` | number | unset | Encourage introducing new topics. |
| `seed` | integer | unset | Fixed random seed, for repeatable replies where the provider supports it. |
| `stop` | string or list of string | unset | Text (or list of texts) at which the model stops writing. |
| `reasoning_effort` | string | unset | How hard a reasoning model should think (`low`, `medium`, `high`), for providers that support it. |
| `response_format` | map of string to any | unset | Ask for a structured reply, e.g. `{"type": "json_object"}`. |
| `extra_body` | map of string to any | empty | Any other provider-specific request fields, passed through unchanged. |
| `thinking` | boolean | unset | Turn a model's thinking mode on or off. Judges default to off. |

## Agent types {#agent-types}

`connection.type` decides how HackAgent talks to the model. It is the field that matters; `provider` is only a label.

**Chat APIs**, reached over HTTP and driven through LiteLLM: `LITELLM`, `OPENAI_SDK`, `OLLAMA`, `LANGCHAIN`. These need an `endpoint`, and an `api_key_env` when the provider requires a key.

**Agents**, driven directly:

| Type | What it is |
|---|---|
| `GOOGLE_ADK` | Native backend for a deployed Google ADK agent server. |
| `CLAUDE_CODE` | Native backend for a locally-installed Claude Code CLI. |
| `CODEX` | Native backend for a locally-installed Codex CLI. |
| `HERMES` | Native backend for a locally-installed Hermes Agent CLI. |
| `WEB` | Native backend that red-teams a website's chatbot by driving the live page. |

:::caution[Not runnable]

`MCP`, `A2A` exist in the format but have no backend, so a campaign using one fails to resolve.

:::

## Examples

**A model served by Ollama on this machine**

```yaml
target:
  name: llama3.2
  connection:
    provider: ollama
    type: OLLAMA
    endpoint: http://localhost:11434
```

**An OpenAI-compatible endpoint, reading the key from the environment**

```yaml
target:
  name: gpt-4o-mini
  connection:
    provider: openai
    type: OPENAI_SDK
    endpoint: https://api.openai.com/v1
    api_key_env: OPENAI_API_KEY
  generation:
    temperature: 0.0
    max_tokens: 512
```

**A coding agent running locally, with no endpoint at all**

```yaml
target:
  name: claude-code
  connection:
    provider: local
    type: CLAUDE_CODE
  options:
    binary: claude
```
